environment: Playwright 1.64.1 / Chromium 156.0.8078.4 headless, macOS arm64 with SwiftShader; phone is the 390 x 844 touch-emulated project at device scale 2
fixture: Disposable in-memory family-mode household. Rowan (owner, adult), Ash (adult) and Wren (child) each sign in with their own virtual passkey. The real kit-list photo reader runs over a fake OpenAI transport (test/helpers/fake-openai.mjs) whose reply is written into the test: 4-person tent 1, sleeping bag 3 (misread), torch 2, stove with no count. The photo is an invented test document, a white card reading "Camping kit (invented test list)" and the four lines, drawn by the test browser. None of this is a person’s list or evidence of how well a model reads a photo.
spec: test/e2e/kit-list.spec.mjs — a family makes its kit list from typed text or a photo, fixes what was misread, and every member reads the saved list
steps: Rowan types the list and chooses Check this list; enters Have 2 for the torch (capture: phone typed draft); Save this list
Start a new list, choose the photo; a reading held until Rowan types is not used; Read the photo with OpenAI again
The draft shows the misread 3 and the blank stove count; Save is refused; then the capture of the draft’s top (desktop photo draft)
Rowan corrects both counts, enters Have 2 for the torch and saves; Ash, Wren and a reload read the same list (captures: desktop saved, phone child view)
Ash edits while Rowan saves a change: Ash keeps their typing, sees the deliberate choice, keeps the draft and saves

images.story: Rowan read the invented test photo with the fake OpenAI transport. The draft, marked not saved, shows the photo beside its first three lines, including the fake reading’s misread count: Need 3 for sleeping bag, where the photo says 2. The stove line, with its blank count flagged "How many are needed? Enter a number.", is further down the draft and outside this capture; the browser test asserts it, and that Save this list was refused just before this capture.
